Q1 integrated. Next question.

**Question:** The spec says an existing *directory* is never a conflict when the archive also stores a directory there (FR-011), but what should happen when the types disagree — the archive holds a file where the destination already has a directory, or the archive holds a directory where the destination already has a file?

**Why it matters:** These collisions can't be resolved by overwriting (you can't replace a non-empty directory with a file), so without a stated rule the implementation would either crash with a raw filesystem error or behave differently with and without `--overwrite`. It also determines whether such a case exits 3 (refused overwrite) or 2 (unusable input), which scripts branch on.

**Recommended:** Option A - A type mismatch isn't something `--overwrite` can consent to, so treating it as unusable input (status 2) regardless of the flag keeps `--overwrite` meaning exactly one thing — "replace an existing regular file" — and keeps status 3 meaning "re-run me with `--overwrite`", which would be false advice here. Caught in the same pre-write pass as FR-020, so nothing is written.

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| A | Type mismatch is always a hard failure: no files written, the offending path named on standard error, exit 2, with or without `--overwrite` |
| B | Treat it like any other conflict: exit 3 without `--overwrite`, and with `--overwrite` delete the existing entry (directory tree included) and write the archive's version |
| C | Exit 3 without `--overwrite`; with `--overwrite`, still fail with exit 2 because the replacement is impossible |
| Short | Provide a different short answer (<=5 words) |

You can reply with the option letter (e.g., "A"), accept the recommendation by saying "yes" or "recommended", or provide your own short answer.
